title: The Sages Who Went to Indra
word: the three doshas as a way of noticing
hookLine: sick sages send one of their own up to Indra, and he brings back the science of life
carry: health is the root of dharma
tomorrow: a boy fasts fifteen days and forgets his Vedas. why?
last: A CLEAR SELF, SENSES AND MIND.

cards: The Charaka Samhita, one of Ayurveda's oldest texts, opens with a problem, not a cure. Great sages, the story says, had given their lives to prayer, study and self-discipline, and illness kept getting in the way.
Bodies gave out before the work was done. So they gathered on a slope of the Himalaya to ask one question: who can help us? And one of them, the sage Bharadvaja, stood up and said: send me.

teach.b: Bharadvaja climbed to Indra, king of the gods, who had received this knowledge, the text says, in a line reaching back to Brahma. Indra taught him the science of life, Ayurveda: ayus, life, and veda, knowledge.
He taught it in three parts: the causes of illness, its signs, and what heals.
Bharadvaja came back down and taught the sages, and one of them, the teacher Atreya, passed it to six students, one of whom first wrote it down. And here is the line the story is built to deliver.

teach.h: HEALTH: THE ROOT OF THE FOUR AIMS.
teach.b: The sages say health is the best root of the four aims of life: dharma, doing what's right; artha, a livelihood; kama, love and joy; and moksha, freedom itself. Illness robs all four.
That's a Hindu teaching, said plainly: the body isn't the enemy of the spiritual life, and caring for it isn't vanity. It's the ground the rest grows from. Even the sages needed it.
So what does this science see?
One verse of the Ashtanga Hridaya, a later classic, gives the doshas a clock: kapha at the beginning, pitta in the middle, vata at the end, of a day, a night, a meal, a whole life.
A slow morning may not be a character flaw; some of it may be the hour. On this path that's a way of noticing, never a diagnosis, and anything that keeps on goes to a doctor. And today?
The night you skip dinner to study, the week you run on four hours of sleep, the sages would say you're digging up the root.

how: Many Hindus see care for the body as part of dharma. Ayurveda, which tradition often links to the Atharva Veda, tells its own beginning as Bharadvaja learning the science of life from Indra for the sake of the sages, and teaches that health is the root of the four aims of life; its dosha clock is used on this path only for noticing.

games.q: what does “the three doshas as a way of noticing” mean?
o: three forces that take turns, in the science Bharadvaja brought down
three daily meals the old texts set out for everyone
three moods a person must fight off through the day

games.q: the science of life — tap the pairs.
p: climbed to Indra for the sages
the four aims health is the root of

s: in the story, the sages wanted health so they could keep praying and studying
illness was getting in the way of their discipline, their study and their lives.
Charaka's sages saw caring for the body as a distraction from the spiritual life
they called health the best root of dharma, artha, kama and moksha.
the Ashtanga Hridaya gives exact hours for each dosha
it says beginning, middle and end, nothing more precise.

games.q: midterms week. you're about to skip dinner and sleep to study harder. by the sages' line, what are you doing?
o: serving dharma: suffering is the point.
digging up the root the four aims grow from.
nothing either way: the body doesn't matter to the spirit.
games.why: health is the root of dharma, artha, kama and moksha. the sages sent Bharadvaja to Indra because illness was blocking their practice.

practice: Sit and feel the body as it is right now: heavy, warm, light or scattered, and notice what part of the day it is. Then, if you pray, thank God for this body, the ground of the four aims, in your own words or a prayer you know.
If you don't pray, thank it anyway. It has carried every good thing you've done.

wordCard.voice: The three doshas, as a way of noticing. Today, the story of how this science came down from Indra, and the line it carries: health is the root of dharma, artha, kama and moksha.

orig.note: Sanskrit: health, freedom from illness. Charaka calls it the best root of the four aims of life.

carryVoice: Your line: health is the root of dharma. Even the sages needed well bodies to pray. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 1 (illness obstructs the sages' austerity, study and life; they gather on the Himalaya; Bharadvaja goes to Indra; the lineage from Brahma; cause, sign and remedy; Atreya and his six students, Agnivesha the first to compose a treatise)
Ashtanga Hridaya, Sutrasthana 1.8 (the doshas rise at the end, middle and beginning of life, day, night and meal: vata, pitta and kapha in turn)
